content:
End of June was the target to have the Preventive Maintenance Push closed out. That came and went yesterday and it is still sitting open.

Brooke started this in early May, HVAC, plumbing and electrical across the whole portfolio, and I have been the QC eye on it. I logged both cluster spot-checks as passing in late May and my read is that my part of it is finished. The crew called the HVAC run wrapped around the same time.

Before I put my name to this closing out, I need to know where every piece of it stands as of today, cluster by cluster, and I need our records saying the same thing. Work out what is actually finished and what is not, and get our tracking to match. Anything still open gets its own tracking item raised, with the person who owns that work named on it. My own spot-check records are part of that, with a short note left on each one saying where it landed and why.

Anything flagged in the field that still needs a tech back onsite belongs in our maintenance ticket log rather than sitting as a tracking item, and put a slot on my calendar to go back out and re-inspect whatever ends up in that follow-up.

Then post where this stands in the channel the push has been running in so the crew is working off the same picture, and draft an email to Brooke, cluster by cluster, with what is open, who is holding it, and what has to happen before this can close.

I do not want Brooke's email written so it can be read either way. If my QC side is a pass, say pass. If it is not, say straight out that my earlier sign-off does not hold and this should not be treated as closeable yet, with the reasons.
I will search Slack
channels, Linear issues, Airtable bases, and local files to locate all information regarding the Preventive Maintenance Push.

parameters.description: Parse and print all issues from first page of Linear issues
parameters.command:
python3 -c "
import json

if json_start != -1:

    for issue in parsed['issues']:

parameters.subject: Preventive Maintenance Push Status & QC Sign-Off Audit — July 1, 2026
parameters.body:
Hi Brooke,

As of today, July 1, 2026, the target closeout date for the portfolio-wide Preventive Maintenance Push has passed. Before putting my name to closing this initiative, I have conducted a thorough audit across all tracking systems, Linear issues, and field inspection records.

To be direct and unequivocal: My QC sign-off for the overall Preventive Maintenance Push is NOT a pass, and my earlier sign-off from late May does NOT hold for closing out this initiative. This push should NOT be treated as closeable yet.

My late-May QC sign-offs were strictly limited to the HVAC spot-checks. The full PM Push scope kicked off in May covers HVAC, Plumbing, and Electrical across the portfolio. Based on current field and tracking records, open work remains in both the West and South clusters.

Here is where every piece stands as of today, cluster by cluster, including open items, work owners, and what must happen before this push can close:

--------------------------------------------------
1. WEST CLUSTER
* Status: OPEN / IN PROGRESS (Linear Issue: OPS-35)
* What is Open: While HVAC condenser cleaning and filter replacements were wrapped in late May (OPS-91), the broader PM Push scope—specifically plumbing and electrical inspections and follow-up repairs across West Cluster properties—remains active and incomplete.
* Work Owners: Lisa Smith (Onsite Lead) & John Smith (Maintenance Execution Lead)
* What Must Happen Before Closeout: Lisa and John must complete all outstanding West Cluster PM walkthroughs, plumbing, and electrical checks, and clear any physical repairs identified during inspections.

--------------------------------------------------
2. SOUTH CLUSTER
* Status: OPEN / PENDING FIELD WORK ORDERS
* What is Open: 
  - HVAC service passed QC spot-checks (OPS-87, OPS-98).
  - Electrical panel inspections were confirmed complete by Patricia Nguyen (OPS-186 updated to Done).
  - Plumbing: Inspections were completed by Carlos Mendez (OPS-97), but two major physical defects requiring tech work back onsite were flagged and remain unexecuted:
    a) Replacement of 2 aging water heaters past serviceable life (Logged in Airtable: MT-2026-1327).
    b) Repair of leaking/damaged hose bibs across multiple units (Logged in Airtable: MT-2026-1328).
* Work Owner: Carlos Mendez (holding vendor quote coordination and repair oversight under Linear issue OPS-1000).
* What Must Happen Before Closeout: Vendor quotes for the 2 water heater replacements must be approved and installed, and hose bib repairs must be executed onsite by maintenance techs per tickets MT-2026-1327 and MT-2026-1328.

--------------------------------------------------
3. NORTH CLUSTER
* Status: COMPLETE
* Completed Scope: HVAC, plumbing, and electrical panel inspections serviced, inspected, and verified (OPS-40, OPS-66, OPS-81). QC spot-checks passed (OPS-87, OPS-98 updated to Done).
* Work Owners / Open Items: None. Fully wrapped.

--------------------------------------------------
4. EAST CLUSTER
* Status: COMPLETE
* Completed Scope: HVAC coil cleaning and filter swaps completed by Elias Navarro (OPS-99) and verified by QC (OPS-108 updated to Done).
* Work Owners / Open Items: None. Fully wrapped.

--------------------------------------------------
QC ACTION PLAN & RE-INSPECTION
To ensure our tracking matches field reality:
- All Linear QC spot-check records (OPS-87, OPS-98, OPS-96, OPS-108, OPS-186, OPS-97) have been updated with explanatory notes and marked Done where work was verified.
- Field repair items requiring a tech back onsite have been moved to our primary maintenance log in Airtable (MT-2026-1327 & MT-2026-1328).
- I have scheduled a slot on my calendar for Thursday, July 2, 2026, 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM to perform an onsite re-inspection walkthrough for the South Cluster plumbing repairs once completed and conduct final field verification for West Cluster.

Once Lisa/John complete the West Cluster PM scope and Carlos gets the South Cluster plumbing work orders executed and cleared, I will perform final re-inspections and issue a full QC pass. Until those items are finished and verified, the PM Push remains open.

Best regards,

Jaime Salinas
Quality Control Inspector
Star Property Management
